reasoning: Both attempts get the main parts right. Each uses Vide springs in component bodies and gives `show` its exit delay, so the picker is kept until it has slid off and the same picker reverses when build mode turns back on. Each blocks clicks while the picker closes with `Interactable` bound to `present`, and each computes the highlight position in offset units. A has nicer polish: tiles scale about their centre, and it adds hover feedback. But A fails StyLua on a line it wrote, and its hand-tracked press state is less robust than B's use of `GuiState`. B passes every check and its press handling is solid. Its one real flaw is cosmetic: tiles shrink toward their top-left corner. Since mergeable, check-clean code counts most, B wins by a narrow margin.

criteria.note: The `scale`, `highlightPosition` and `panelPosition` springs are created in the `tile` and `blockPicker` bodies and bound to properties; nothing is created inside a binding.

criteria.criterion: Closing slide plays / opening moves panel
criteria.note: `blockPicker` returns `panel, EXIT_DURATION`, and `return BlockPicker({...})` passes both values on to `show`; `panelPosition` follows `present`, which moves the panel itself.
`show` keeps the same picker if build mode turns back on during the exit delay, so the spring reverses from where it is, and `Interactable = shown` stops a closing picker from taking clicks.
`tileOffset(index)` uses `(index - 1) * (TILE_SIZE + TILE_GAP)` inside the padded panel; it never reads `AbsolutePosition`.

`InputBegan`/`InputEnded` handle MouseButton1 and Touch, and the button is centred in a slot so it scales about its middle; a touch dragged off the tile relies on `InputEnded` still firing to reset `pressed`.
Selection, placement and scaling keep working, but StyLua fails on the single-line `Size = UDim2.fromOffset(...)` that this attempt wrote.
The `scale`, `position` and `highlightPosition` springs are created in component bodies and bound to properties.

criteria.criterion: Closing slide plays / opening moves panel
criteria.note: `show` returns `BlockPicker.new(...), BlockPicker.ExitDuration`, and `position` follows `Present`, which moves the panel itself.
`show` keeps the same picker during the exit delay, so the spring reverses, and `Interactable = props.Present` stops clicks while the picker closes.
`changed("GuiState", guiState)` reacts to Press for mouse and touch alike and is robust, but the `UIScale` on a top-left-anchored tile makes it shrink toward its corner instead of its centre.
All checks pass, and changing the module to return `{ new = ..., ExitDuration = ... }` is matched by the update in `Main`.

strengths: Shrinks the tile about its centre by placing a centred button inside a slot frame
Adds hover feedback and hides the highlight when no tile matches the selection
Hands the exit delay to `show` cleanly through a second return value
weaknesses: StyLua check fails on its own code
Tracks press state by hand with `InputBegan`/`InputEnded`, which is less robust than reading `GuiState`

strengths: Reads press state from `GuiState`, which is simple and robust for mouse and touch
Sets a clear `EXIT_DURATION` that matches a critically damped slide
weaknesses: The press scale shrinks toward the tile's top-left corner rather than its centre
`indexOf` silently falls back to index 1 for an unknown selection
